bottleneck.label: Calculator
bottleneck.title: Bottleneck Analysis
bottleneck.subtitle: A “bottleneck” is when one part (CPU or GPU) can't keep up with the other, capping your frame rate. Pair a CPU with a GPU to see if they're well matched — and the FPS you can expect across resolutions and game types.
bottleneck.verdictBalancedDesc: Your CPU and GPU are well matched — neither noticeably holds the other back.
bottleneck.verdictCpuDesc: Your CPU is the limiter here. It shows up most at low resolution / high frame rates; raising resolution or settings shifts more work to the GPU.
bottleneck.verdictGpuDesc: Your GPU is the limiter here — normal and usually ideal for gaming. Lower the resolution/settings or enable upscaling to lift FPS.
bottleneck.matrixHint: Each cell shows the bottleneck % and which part limits it. Green = balanced, red = a strong bottleneck.

upscalingNote.enableUpscaling: Enable {tech} (Quality mode) to lift frame rates at {resolution} with minimal visual loss.

tip.esportsShadows: Lower shadows and reflections to maximise frame rate and reduce input latency.
tip.fourKTextures: Texture quality is nearly free at 4K with enough VRAM — keep it high.

streaming.title: Streaming Suite
streaming.whatIsThis: New to streaming? This tool tells you exactly what to type into OBS or Streamlabs so your live stream looks good and doesn't buffer — based on your GPU, platform, and internet speed. No jargon needed.
streaming.signInSuffix: with a Pro plan to configure streaming.
streaming.gpuBrandHelp: Your graphics card maker — decides which built-in video encoder you'll use.
streaming.resolutionHelp: How sharp your stream looks to viewers.
streaming.fpsHelp: Frames per second — 60 is smooth, 30 saves bandwidth.
streaming.uploadHelp: Your internet UPLOAD speed (not download). Check it at fast.com and read the 'upload' number.
streaming.downscaleNote: You picked {input}, but streaming at {res} will look cleaner with your upload/platform limits.
streaming.quality_good_desc: Very watchable; slightly soft in fast motion.
streaming.quality_limited_desc: Noticeably soft — try a lower resolution or a better upload.
streaming.impactsFpsNote: Encoded by your CPU (x264), so it can lower your in-game FPS. A GPU hardware encoder is gentler.
streaming.noImpactFpsNote: Encoded by your GPU's dedicated video chip, so it barely affects your game's FPS.
streaming.errProFeature: Streaming suite is a Pro feature — upgrade on Pricing.

encoderReason.nvenc: NVENC (Turing+) offloads encoding from the CPU with near-x264-medium quality.
encoderReason.amf: AMD AMF/VCE hardware encoding frees the CPU; use the latest drivers for best quality.
encoderReason.quicksync: Intel Quick Sync provides efficient hardware encoding, ideal for single-PC setups.
encoderReason.x264: No hardware encoder detected — x264 (CPU) encoding. Needs spare CPU headroom.

warning.uploadLimit: Your upload ({upload} Mbps) limits quality — recommended bitrate capped at {recommended} kbps.
warning.platformCap: {platform} caps ingest at {platformMax} kbps; {resolution}@{fps} would ideally use {ideal} kbps.
warning.twitch4k: Twitch does not officially support 4K ingest — consider 1080p/1440p.
